solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: They may be shot close to camp in attacks

indicators.note: one thing set in another is placed inside it, so the camp letter goes inside the word for attacks

parts.note: raids are sudden attacks

indicators.note: 'close to' keeps only the last letter of 'camp'

parts.note: the final letter of camp

explanation.surface: Soldiers come under fire near their camp during enemy assaults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests gunfire, but canoeists and rafters shoot rapids by riding down them.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapids are fast, rough stretches of river, and to shoot them is to travel down them in a boat.

clue.text: Confine oneself to our boss's articles, maybe, further tailored?

parts.note: articles are things that are read
to do just one thing is to confine oneself to it
on a newspaper, the boss is the editor, Ed

explanation.surface: A newspaper writer wonders whether to read only the editor's pieces after another rewrite.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes the phrase 'read just Ed': read only the editor's articles. The question mark flags this indirect route.
explanation.definitionFit: Readjusted means altered again, and tailored further means adjusted once more to fit.

clue.text: Twice a year, left from Rome?

indicators.note: twice tells us to write the abbreviation two times in a row

parts.note: PA is per annum, a year
the same abbreviation again
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone leaves Rome two times a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From Rome' is a hint: the papacy is based in Rome, so the question mark warns this is a loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Papal means coming from the Pope, whose seat is the Vatican in Rome.

clue.text: Blank flier secretary placed in study …

indicators.note: placed in means put inside, so the pair goes inside the study word

parts.note: a den is a private study
a flier is a leaflet advertisement, an ad
PA stands for personal assistant, a secretary

explanation.surface: An expressionless pilot's secretary is put in an office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests an aviator but means a printed leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan face is blank, showing no emotion.

clue.text: Screening of material from a film finally is repeated in French

indicators.note: repeated tells us to write the French word a second time straight after the first

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the last letter of film
est is French for 'is'
the same French word again

explanation.surface: A cinema censor screens material from a film, a phrase repeated in French subtitles.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ames test is a laboratory screen that checks whether a chemical causes genetic mutations; 'screening' is lab testing, not cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ames test is a standard biological assay used to screen chemical substances for their capacity to cause mutations.

clue.text: … which one drinking coffee raises?

parts.note: surface reading: a coffee drinker lifts something to the lips
setter's reading: the drinker's cup is held aloft, giving a phrase meaning to study hard

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the 3 down clue, whose last word, study, completes the definition: to mug up is to cram.
explanation.definitionFit: To mug up is British slang for studying a subject intensively, typically just before an exam.

clue.text: Suddenly hard to keep quiet

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so the quiet letter goes inside

parts.note: steely means hard as steel
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: Without warning it became difficult to stay silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope that rises steeply climbs abruptly, so suddenly is a fair synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Confidentially French resistance moving in to record intelligence

indicators.note: the resistance symbol shifts one place towards the middle of its word, a small rearrangement

parts.note: to enter data is to record it
nous is common sense or intelligence

explanation.surface: The French Resistance secretly moves in to gather intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French resistance' reads as the wartime Resistance; here French belongs to the definition and resistance is the electrical symbol R.
explanation.definitionFit: Entre nous is a French phrase meaning between ourselves, said of something told in confidence.

clue.text: What cashier has to work up to

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cash register or money drawer
second meaning: until, as in 'wait up to six'

explanation.surface: A shop assistant has to keep working until closing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To work' is also a third meaning: to till the soil is to cultivate it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for a cash drawer and a preposition meaning until, as well as a verb for working land.

clue.text: Salt tablet with nail on top

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so this element heads the column

parts.note: a pin is a slim nail
NaCl is the chemical formula for common salt
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: A salt tablet comes with a nail stuck on top of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt tablet' reads as one thing, but the chemistry formula and a drug-slang letter are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnacle is the highest point or peak, so it is the top.

clue.text: Fetching a soft sort of green heather

parts.note: taken as written
p (piano) is the musical marking for soft
pea green is a shade of green
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: A soft green heather makes an attractive plant for the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Ling is the common heather of British moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetching and appealing are both adjectives for something attractive or charming.

clue.text: Praise from partner once was effective, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of that phrase's word is dropped

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
something that told had an effect, as in 'the strain told on him'

explanation.surface: Compliments from a former partner once worked, more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Native of Mexico in NJ: People appear confused!

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled out of their proper order and must be put right

parts.note: all fourteen letters used as written

explanation.surface: Residents of New Jersey look bewildered by a Mexican immigrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native of Mexico' paints a person, but it is a plant: the jalapeño originates there.
explanation.definitionFit: The jalapeño is a hot chilli pepper first grown in Mexico, named after the city of Xalapa.

clue.text: After a failure, one has to be tolerant

parts.note: per means a or each, as in miles per hour
a miss is a failure to hit
one gives I, and has gives the contraction 've: I've

explanation.surface: After a setback, one must be forgiving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After a' is read as a single item, the PER of 'per annum'; the elements then follow in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Permissive means allowing much freedom, a close synonym of tolerant.

clue.text: One could go off father getting close to son!

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a male parent

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of son

explanation.surface: A father about to lose his temper as he gets near his son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go off' suggests an explosion of temper; an alarm goes off too.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is an alarm or warning device, and alarms are said to go off when they sound.

clue.text: In the act of re-forming diamonds hardened

indicators.note: re-forming means shaping again, so these letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds
taken as written

explanation.surface: A jeweller caught in the middle of reshaping hardened diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: To be caught red-handed is to be caught in the act of wrongdoing, so the idiom means in the act.

clue.text: Youngster taking short vacation in extra small location

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, or a junior Scout

indicators.note: placed in something means set inside it, so the holiday word sits within the extra

parts.note: a bye is a cricket extra, a run scored without the batter hitting the ball
hol is a clipped form of holiday

explanation.surface: A child going on a brief holiday somewhere extremely small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extra small' reads as one phrase meaning tiny, but 'extra' is the cricket term and 'small location' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cubby-hole is a small snug space or compartment, so it is a small place by definition.

clue.text: What could be worn by pool club personnel: medal

definitions.text: What could be worn by pool

parts.note: a bat is a club for hitting a ball
HR is human resources, the personnel department
the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, awarded as a medal

explanation.surface: A list of items for the swimming club's staff and their medals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pool club' sounds like one swimming club, but the definition ends at pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathrobe is a loose towelling gown, the sort of thing worn beside a swimming pool.

clue.text: Women tend to get fixed income

indicators.note: something that has to get fixed is broken and must be rebuilt in a working order

parts.note: both words used letter for letter

explanation.surface: Women usually end up on a fixed income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixed income' looks like a finance phrase, but 'fixed' belongs with the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An endowment is a fund given to an institution, providing it with a regular income.

clue.text: Acquire sports car at ridiculously cheap price — a bit of a flyer!

parts.note: to win something is to acquire it
GT (gran turismo) marks a sports car
one penny, written 1P, read as IP

explanation.surface: Buy a sports car for almost nothing: someone is on to a winner.
explanation.walkthrough: The numeral 1 doubles as the letter I, so a one-penny price gives the two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A wing tip is the outer end of an aircraft's or bird's wing, part of something that flies.

clue.text: According to report, not out always to be brief

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so we want a phrase that is spoken the same way

parts.note: not out means in, and only some of the time rather than always

explanation.surface: A batsman reported not out every time wants to keep it short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not out' is a cricket phrase but here simply means in; 'not always' becomes 'in some' cases.
explanation.definitionFit: In sum means in short or to summarise, a phrase used when being brief.

clue.text: Cool present for one getting passionate

parts.note: in means fashionable or cool
the present is one example of a grammatical tense

explanation.surface: A trendy gift for someone who is becoming ardent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift, but 'for one' marks it as an example: the present tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense feelings are strong and passionate, so the adjectives match.

clue.text: Potentially 14 different people in pursuit of British film studio

indicators.note: pursuing something means following behind it, so these letters come after the abbreviation

parts.note: the answer to 14 across sounds an alert, so it is potentially a warner
Br is the abbreviation for British
others are different people

explanation.surface: Alarms, maybe, and strangers chase a Briton to a film studio.
explanation.walkthrough: SIREN at 14 is a warning device, so something that warns: a warner.
explanation.definitionFit: Warner Brothers is the Hollywood company founded by four Warner siblings, one of the biggest film studios.

clue.text: Chance briefly to catch very loud bits of tune

indicators.note: catching something means holding it inside, so the loud letters go within
briefly means cut short, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: a risk is a chance taken
ff (fortissimo) is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A quick opportunity to capture some very loud snatches of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Riffs are short repeated phrases in pop or jazz, which are bits of a tune.

clue.text: Knight once held up by Jedi, clearly

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
held means contained, so the letters are found inside the following words

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: An old-style knight is detained by a Star Wars Jedi, obviously.
explanation.walkthrough: A Jedi is a knight in Star Wars, which makes the surface feel all of a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: El Cid was an eleventh-century Castilian knight and military leader, the hero of Spanish epic.

clue.text: Stick book in the post

parts.note: to jam is to stick fast
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: Put a book into the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like the mail, but it is a wooden upright.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamb is the vertical side post of a door or window frame.

clue.text: Tried out an oddly regressive inspection

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the kept letters are read from right to left
oddly points to the letters in odd-numbered positions, first, third, fifth and so on

parts.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: Something tested in a strangely backward-looking review.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is an official inspection, especially of accounts.

clue.text: Figures chap in charge can ring back with story

parts.note: a fib is a story, a small lie

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so this group is written from right to left

parts.note: IC is the abbreviation for in charge
taken as written
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A man in authority can phone back with an excuse about the numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: The story element comes first in the answer though it is last in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Fibonacci was the medieval Italian mathematician whose name is attached to a famous sequence of numbers.

clue.text: Does like time pursuing friend in US city

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the time letter is placed at the end

parts.note: bud is American slang for a friend
to ape is to imitate
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Female deer that love time chasing a friend around an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like the female deer, but it is the verb: someone who apes does like another.
explanation.definitionFit: Budapest is the capital city of Hungary.

clue.text: From hearing, cycle to market

indicators.note: taking a word from hearing means going by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: to pedal is to ride a bicycle

explanation.surface: A rider hears it is a good idea to cycle to the market.
explanation.definitionFit: To peddle goods is to sell them, as a hawker or street trader does.
